key_insight: Precursor-ratio control of chloride vacancies enables forming-free, gradual resistive switching in lead-free KCuCl3-x memristors for neuromorphic computing, rather than solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Tuning vacancy concentration balances ionic mobility and defect controllability to improve analog synaptic behavior in lead-free memristive devices.
method: Vary precursor ratios during wet chemical synthesis of KCuCl3-x thin films.
Evaluate vacancy-dependent electronic structure and switching in W/KCuCl3-x/FTO memristors.
Use measured conductance characteristics as synaptic weights in neural-network simulations.
evidence_signal: At an optimal vacancy concentration of approximately 1.3 × 10^21 cm^-3, devices show highly linear potentiation/depression and pulse endurance above 10^4 cycles; simulations achieve 98.96% MNIST and 91.82% Fashion-MNIST accuracy.
watch_item: Recognition results are simulation-based; the abstract does not establish integrated-array performance, device variability, or measured energy savings.
paper_title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
